numbers of gamma interferon-producing cells reactive to ESat-6 antigen are increased in recent converters, in tuberculosis patients, but not in unimmunized or Mycobacterum bovis BCG vaccinated healthy donors.

the numbers of gamma interferon- (IFN- γ-)producing cells reactive with early secreted antigenic target 6 (ESAT-6) and purified protein derivative (PPD) are increased in recent converters, as well as in patients with active tuberculosis, but not in healthy unvaccinated donors and in Mycobacterium tuberculosis-vaccinated healthy volunteers, and ESAT-6 reactive IFN-γ- producing cells in recent converters recognize similar synthetic peptides as do ES

the numbers of gamma interferon-producing cells reactive to ESAS-6 antigen are increased in recent converters, as well as in tuberculosis patients, but not in healthy unvaccinated and Mycobacterium tuberculosis BCG-vaccined individuals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the immune response in tuberculosis, in particular with the study of T-cell responses in patients with tuberculosis.
the development of a new diagnostic test, based on a novel immunological assay for tuberculosis, using the ESAT-6 gene.

the study of the immune response of tuberculosis patients, recent converters to PPD positivity and healthy donors to the 6-kD early secretory antigenic target (ESAT-6) and the 10-kD culture filtrate protein (CFP-10) antigens.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is a strong correlation between the number of ESAT- 6-reactive IFNgamma+ cells and the presence of tuberculosis.
there is no evidence that the use of BCG vaccination is associated with an increase in the risk of developing tuberculosis in children and adolescents.

the use of the ESAT-6 and/or CFP-10 peptides in the IFN-γ release assays is a useful tool in the detection of active tuberculosis in patients who have been BCG vaccinated, but not in the detection of latent infection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ESAT-6 and PPD are potential candidates for use in detection and control of early and active tuberculosis.
ESAT-6 and culture filtrate protein 10 (CFP-10) are the best candidates for a new diagnostic tool for tuberculosis.
the ESAT-6 and culture filtrate protein-10 (CFP-10) genes of Mycobacterium tuberculosis (M. tuberculosis) are located within a 9.5-kb DNA fragment that is absent in the M. bovis BCG vaccine strain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ESAT-6 and CFP-10 antigens are highly immunogenic and can be used for the detection of early, subclinical, and active TB.
the ESAT-6 protein, which is expressed by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, can be used to identify people infected with the organism.
ESAT-6 and PPD-specific IFN-γ-secreting cells can be used for detection of active and subclinical tuberculosis.
